Pricing & Inventory Dataset Preparation Report

SyncGuard AI · Week 1 deliverable

Team 14 · generated November 22, 2026

1. Objective

Prepare a documented, clean baseline of pricing and inventory synchronization records so an autoencoder can learn what normal syncing looks like. This report covers the dataset, the problems found, how each was fixed, channel-level statistics, visualizations of normal behavior, and the engineered features.

2. Dataset

No public dataset of master-vs-channel sync logs exists, so a realistic synthetic dataset was generated (data_generator.py). It simulates 30 products sold on 3 channels (Amazon, Shopify, eBay) with hourly sync records from 2026-01-01 to 2026-01-30. A small share of rows (2%) has injected errors (price mismatch, decimal slip, stale sync, stock drift, oversell risk) so detection quality can be measured. Legitimate-but-unusual behaviour is included too: promotions (the master price drops and each channel catches up an hour later), bulk inventory deliveries and occasional sync retries. Operational messiness (duplicates, gaps, impossible values) was also added to mimic a real export. A real dataset can be dropped in without code changes beyond the loader.

Column Meaning
timestamp When the sync happened
sku Product code
channel Sales channel (Shopify, Amazon, eBay)
master_price / channel_price Price in the master system vs shown on the channel
master_stock / channel_stock Stock in the master system vs shown on the channel
units_sold Units sold in that hour
sync_delay_min Minutes since the channel was last updated
sync_attempts / sync_status Attempts the sync needed, and the status the integration reported (success, retry, failed)
is_anomaly / anomaly_type Injected-error labels, used only for evaluation, never for training
65,059Raw rows
64,800Clean rows
30Products
3Channels

3. Inspection and cleaning

Issue found Rows Treatment
Rows missing timestamp, product, channel or master values 0 Dropped: cannot be interpreted
Duplicate rows (same product, channel, time) 259 Kept first copy
Negative / zero stock or price 129 Treated as missing, then imputed
Missing channel price 259 Master price × the channel's normal ratio
Missing channel stock 259 Fair share of master stock
Missing sync delay 259 Median delay of that channel
Row order - Sorted by product, channel, time (needed for change features)
Imputation uses values that look normal, so a repaired row is never mistaken for an anomaly just because it was damaged. The trade-off is that a real error sitting in a damaged row is lost; this affects well under 1% of rows.

Each channel has its own stable pricing ratio to the master (for example Amazon about +3%, eBay about −2%), which is why the model learns a per-channel baseline instead of using one global rule.

4b. Encoding categorical and timestamp attributes

Attribute Numeric representation
sku, channel Category codes and one-hot channel columns
sync_status success = 0, retry = 1, failed = 2
timestamp Hour of day and day of week as sine/cosine pairs (23:00 sits next to 00:00), plus epoch seconds
update interval Minutes since the previous update of the same product and channel, log-scaled

The fully encoded table is saved as data/processed/encoded_sync_data.csv. The model learns from the engineered features below, standardized (mean 0, spread 1) so no feature dominates.

5. Normal pricing and inventory behavior

Price ratio by channel: tight, stable bands.

Channel stock tracks its fair share of master stock.

Sync delay: most syncs complete within minutes, with a thin tail.

6. Feature engineering

Feature How it is computed Why it matters
price_diff_pct (channel price / master price) / channel's normal ratio − 1 Catches wrong or stale prices and decimal slips
stock_diff_pct (channel stock − fair share of master stock) / fair share Catches inventory that drifted from the master
sync_delay_log log(1 + minutes since last sync) Catches late or stopped integrations (log tames the long tail)
stock_cover_hours log(1 + channel stock / units sold per hour) Catches oversell risk: stock running out faster than expected
price_change_pct channel price % change minus master price % change since the previous record (capped) Catches sudden price jumps the master did not make
stock_change_pct channel stock % change minus master stock % change since the previous record (capped) Catches sudden stock jumps the master did not make (shared restocks cancel out)
sync_attempts_log log(1 + number of attempts the sync needed) Catches integrations that keep retrying
update_gap_log log(1 + minutes since the previous update of the same product and channel) Catches irregular update intervals and missing updates
sync_status_code 0 = success, 1 = retry, 2 = failed (categorical, encoded as a number) Catches syncs the integration itself reported as failing

Scaled feature distributions: normal rows (grey) versus injected errors (red).

Correlations between features.

7. Output

A cleaned file (data/processed/sync_data.csv), a learned per-channel baseline, a fitted scaler and a scaled feature table form the baseline dataset handed to the modeling stage. The encoded dataset is saved alongside it.
